subject: Re: Redwood vs Hyperscaler model eval - next steps & prompt set

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Redwood vs Hyperscaler model eval - next steps

Hi Maria -

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned:

What we heard:
- Acme AI is evaluating model quality (hallucination, instruction-following) and unit economics for a customer-facing assistant.
- Main comparators: Bedrock (Anthropic/Claude) and Vertex AI (Open-style models) - you mentioned latency and hallucination rate are top priorities.

Proposed next steps:
1) You send the eval prompt set and any blacklisted terms / policy constraints (you mentioned a set of ~1k prompts).
2) We run a side-by-side quality run: Redwood hosted runtime vs Bedrock vs Vertex using your prompts. We'll return hallucination rates, instruction-following scores, and top-level regression checks.
3) We'll also provide cost/latency baselines (tokens/sec, median latency) and suggested config (quantization, batching) to hit your SLOs.

Deliverables & timeline:
- Initial quality report (hallucination + instruction-following): 5 business days after receiving prompts.
- Cost/latency baseline and config suggestions: 7 business days.

Attachments: acme-poc-requirements.pdf (I attached the short template we discussed to make sure we capture your constraints).

If that aligns, can you share the prompt file and any restricted outputs? Also, is the eval allowed to run on your real user data or should we use the synthetic set you mentioned?

Thanks - happy to jump on a 30-min sync if helpful.

Rachel Kim
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Redwood vs Hyperscaler model eval - next steps

Thanks Rachel -

That looks good. Attaching the prompt set (acme-eval-prompts-v1.json) and a short doc with our policy constraints (sensitive_topics.md). For the prompts:
- ~1,050 items, mixed QA + instruction-following + multi-turn snippets.
- Please run against synthetic data only (do not include PII). We can provide obfuscated user examples if needed.

A couple of clarifications:
- For hallucination checks, we'd like a binary flag per response + a short justification (1-2 lines) where the model hallucinates facts about the customer domain.
- We care about output safety: any generation flagged for policy violation should be separately counted.

Can you confirm you'll include exact prompt/response pairs and the model config used (model name, temperature, max_tokens, truncation behavior)?

Appreciate it - looking forward to the baseline.

Best,
Maria Gonzalez
Head of Product, Acme AI
maria.gonzalez@acme.ai

Subject: Fwd: Acme AI eval prompts - action items (DEAL-2026-078)

Team - forwarding Acme's prompt set and constraints. High priority POC for a potential Dedicated deal. Summary & asks below.

Summary:
- Customer: Acme AI (Head of Product: Maria)
- Scope: Run 1.05k prompt set against Redwood hosted runtimes and two hyperscaler endpoints (Bedrock, Vertex). Collect hallucination flag, short justification for hallucination, instruction-following score, and safety violations. Customer requires synthetic-only data.

Asks (owners & timeline):
- Marissa: Lead the quality evaluation. Run the prompt set against: Redwood production-mostly-default config (redwood/meta-x-1-base-like), Bedrock_{anthropic-claude-2}, Vertex_{gpt-family}. Produce per-prompt metrics + aggregate (hallucination rate, avg instruction-follow score). Target: initial run + analysis in 5 business days. Include a simple regression check vs our last benchmark (May 2026).
- Neha: Define the scoring rubric and verification process for hallucination flags (I want a reproducible rule + a short justification template for the human reviewer). Also prepare sampling strategy for manual review (n=200).
- Aditya: Capture latency and cost baseline. For each endpoint capture median latency, p95, tokens/sec, and estimated token cost for a 100k query month. Suggest config knobs (batch size, quantization) and expected % cost reduction. Target: 7 business days.

Attachments to include in the run: acme-eval-prompts-v1.json, sensitive_topics.md (customer-provided), acme-poc-requirements.pdf (we provided).

Related links: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/67890 (deal record)

Please confirm and call out any blockers. I'll coordinate a brief sync with Maria next Tuesday if we need clarifications.

Rachel Kim
